ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: the left side of the attached figure is an AC power supply supplying power through the transformer secondary side, and the secondary-side voltage is labeled U2; the right side is a bridge rectifier circuit composed of four thyristors VT1, VT2, VT3, VT4, the output end is connected to a load, the load side is labeled with output voltage Ud and current id, and resistor R is also marked. Then reason: according to the problem and the specified method, treat it as a single-phase fully controlled bridge rectifier circuit with a resistive load. It is known that U2 = 200 V, triggering angle alpha = 30°. The formula for the average output voltage of a single-phase fully controlled bridge with resistive load is Ud = 0.9 U2 (1 + cos alpha) / 2. Substituting cos 30° = 0.866 gives Ud = 0.9 × 200 × (1 + 0.866) / 2 = 167.94 V, approximately 168 V.

method.method_draft: First describe the image as a transformer secondary supplying a four-SCR bridge and a right-side resistive dc load. From the text take U2 = 200 V and alpha = 30 degrees. Model the secondary voltage as u2 = sqrt(2)U2 sin(theta). For a resistive load, each half-cycle conducts from the firing angle alpha until the natural zero crossing, so average the output waveform over the two symmetric conduction intervals: Ud = (sqrt(2)U2/pi)(1+cos alpha). Substitute the values to obtain Ud ≈ 167.9 V, rounded to 168 V.

planner_metadata.image_role: Use the image to infer the bridge conduction structure: four controlled devices VT1–VT4 form two diagonal conducting pairs connected to the transformer secondary u2, and the output voltage Ud is measured down the right-hand load branch labeled R/Ud/id.
planner_metadata.text_role: Use the text to select the resistive-load case and to obtain the firing angle and rms secondary voltage. The given R = 10 ohm could later convert Ud to Id, but it is not necessary for the average-voltage integral; I2/Id is also extraneous for this calculation.
planner_metadata.knowledge_role: For a resistive load in a phase-controlled bridge, current follows the applied rectified secondary voltage only after each firing angle. With u2 = Vm sin theta and Vm = sqrt(2) U2, the positive output intervals are alpha to pi and pi+alpha to 2pi. Average over one period: Ud = (1/(2pi))[integral_alpha^pi Vm sin theta dtheta + integral_{pi+alpha}^{2pi}(-Vm sin theta)dtheta] = Vm/pi*(1+cos alpha). Then Vm = sqrt(2)*200 V and alpha = 30 degrees, giving Ud = (sqrt(2)*200/pi)*(1+0.866) ≈ 168 V.
